stories.notes: Multi-platform live preview feature with empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Requires openspec to elaborate requirements and define AC, followed by speckit to harden with testability, security, and edge-case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — live preview does not exist in the codebase. The attachment point is useContent (236 callers), the single funnel through which all Contentstack content flows. Modifying how it resolves content (preview vs published) propagates to every consumer without touching them individually. Secondary attachment points are the Next.js API routes or middleware that proxy CMS requests, since preview content requires different request parameters than published content.

Openspec provided an empty AC list with valuable architectural notes about useContent being the single funnel (236 callers) and API routes/middleware as secondary attachment points. I created all 12 ACs from scratch based on the story title, description, and technical file references. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the core toggle behavior through useContent; (2) AC-3/AC-4 define preview activation/deactivation as observable outcomes without prescribing the mechanism; (3) AC-5 addresses authorization — preview content must not leak to unauthorized users; (4) AC-6 covers graceful degradation on preview API failure; (5) AC-7 requires a visual preview indicator for clarity and compliance; (6) AC-8 addresses real-time live preview updates (the 'live' in the title); (7) AC-9 ensures zero-touch propagation to all 236 useContent consumers; (8) AC-10 ensures the API request is observably different in preview mode; (9) AC-11 ensures preview mode persists across navigation; (10) AC-12 covers the ContentstackLink component called out in technical notes. CAVEAT: Without reading the actual file contents (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, etc.), I cannot verify exact API signatures, existing query parameter structures, or whether Contentstack's Live Preview SDK is already partially integrated. The ACs are written at the behavior level to remain valid regardless of implementation details, but precision around what 'preview-specific parameters' means (AC-10) would improve with file access.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline flow broke down: coordinatorNotes explicitly tasked openspec with 'elaborate requirements and define AC,' but openspec produced only architectural attachment-point notes (acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0) without authoring any acceptance criteria. Speckit then had to create all 12 ACs from scratch, performing openspec's intended role. The 12 ACs were never hardened by a second-pass review since speckit authored them in the first pass — the collaborative two-stage design (elaborate → harden) collapsed into a single-stage effort. Both agents did add non-overlapping value (openspec: useContent funnel analysis with 236 callers, secondary attachment points; speckit: comprehensive behavioral ACs covering authorization, degradation, real-time updates, zero-touch propagation), but the quality of the pipeline output is compromised. Speckit's own caveat about lacking file access to verify exact API signatures and Contentstack Live Preview SDK integration status introduces precision risk, particularly around AC-10 ('preview-specific parameters'). Human review should validate the 12 ACs against actual codebase APIs and consider re-running openspec with explicit instructions to author ACs before speckit hardening.
